A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPATIA study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional appendix material in v3.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original morphology-generation, prediction, clustering, and ablation results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 4–7.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results, reevaluates cross-platform clustering, and reports additional scaling, initialization, and pairing-corruption results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The hierarchical architecture, OT pairing, flow matching, and morphology-alignment objectives remain equivalent. However, v3 removes v2's explicit descriptions of platform tokens, embedding orthogonality, and knowledge distillation without explaining whether these training components were eliminated or merely omitted from the description. An actual method change is therefore unresolved.

E1.justification: Table 12 adds a cross-slide corruption scenario using mismatched targets from different slides of the same donor; v2 tested within-slide corruption. The MIST collection, biological transition tasks, and other benchmark coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: PCA is removed from the numerical cross-platform comparison in Table 2, although it remains in Figure 5 and Table 4. Other reported comparator memberships are retained. CellPLM disappears from Section 4.3's comparator prose but had no Table 2 result row in either version.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 explicitly reports reevaluating clustering with the best Leiden resolution selected from shared candidates. Appendix F adds controlled 86M-versus-307M encoder comparisons and stronger corruption settings. The newly stated 70/10/20 split ratio documents an existing donor-disjoint evaluation rather than establishing that its splits changed.

E4.justification: Appendix F introduces encoder-capacity analysis, quantifies the pretrained-versus-scratch comparison previously described in Appendix A, and extends OT corruption from 10–20% within-slide to 30–40% within-slide and 20% cross-slide. Appendix E also adds silhouette-based batch diagnostics. These substantially expand evidence about capacity, initialization, and weak-pairing limitations.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 2 gain per-result uncertainty values, with Table 2 explicitly reporting mean and standard deviation over five seeds. v2 already reported three-run averages, biomarker standard-deviation bounds, and seed information in Appendix A. The unchanged Table 1 means do not establish additional generation runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the clustering scores under the revised protocol: SPATIA's Xenium ARI changes from 0.668 to 0.735 and CosMx ARI from 0.565 to 0.542. Tables 10–12 add substantive findings, including worse clustering for ViT-Large than Base and improved clustering with pretrained initialization. Table 1 means and Tables 3–5 remain unchanged; v3 also removes the erroneous claim of a 0.27 loss reduction beside Table 5.

T1.justification: The OT formulation, flow objectives, reconstruction losses, and Algorithm 1 retain equivalent mathematics. The explicit normalized confidence-weight formula added as v3 Equation 4 already appears in v2 Appendix C.3, Equation 13; its inclusion is explanatory rather than a new derivation.

C1.justification: v3 removes invariant learning through embedding independence and platform tokens from the main contribution list and reframes abstract-level generation as modeling target-state morphology distributions. The central joint predictive/generative contribution, dataset scale, and claimed 8% generative and up-to-3% predictive improvements persist.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly limits inference to unseen control cells within observed transition families. It also adds explanations linking larger-encoder underperformance to transfer and overfitting, cautions that aggressive batch correction can erase biological structure, and interprets stronger pairing-corruption results. Population-level rather than same-cell transitions were already explained in v2's appendix.

D1.justification: v3 adds project/code links, the exact 70/10/20 split ratio, baseline-specific conditioning interfaces, ImageNet-1k initialization information, and the 2,000-cells-per-dataset batch-analysis sample size. Cell resizing, padding, donor separation, hardware, and training-budget details were already present in v2's appendices.

R1.justification: v3 removes two Li et al. 2024 works about cryptocurrency and digital assets that v2 cited in the introduction. Appendix E adds limited positioning alongside scGPT-spatial. Consolidating duplicate scFoundation references is bibliographic cleanup, not removal of distinct prior work.

P1.justification: v3 revises the abstract, contribution list, training paragraph, and conclusion, and brings several appendix explanations into the main text. It also updates affiliations, publication information, acknowledgments, and disclosures. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 8 and Tables 10–12, reformats Tables 1–2 to accommodate uncertainty values, and adjusts figure captions, including clarifying what the target images represent in Figure 4. Existing figures and tables are retained with limited resizing and relocation rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessability through uncertainty reporting, quantitative evidence about encoder and pairing limitations, clearer conditioning descriptions, and additional reproducibility information. These extend an already substantial evaluation. The unexplained removal of platform-training descriptions and the retained overbroad clustering discussion—SPATIA still trails competitors on CosMx NMI in Table 2—limit the overall gain.
